key_insight: Targeting uncertain flow-regime boundaries with new simulations improves ensemble predictions and supports confidence-aware inverse design of microdroplet generators.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps identify device configurations that meet target droplet sizes while reducing reliance on costly multiphase-flow simulations.
method: Train neural network ensembles on high-fidelity Volume-of-Fluid simulations to predict flow regimes and droplet diameters.
Use regime consensus and diameter coefficient of variation to guide physics-informed enrichment near transitions and address class imbalance.
Apply constrained Particle Swarm Optimization to balance target-size accuracy, predictive confidence, and physical consistency.
evidence_signal: On independent test datasets, enrichment nearly doubled the fraction of diameter predictions with 0–3% error and substantially reduced cases above 10% error.
watch_item: Ensemble agreement alone does not guarantee accuracy outside the sampled design space; unfamiliar configurations may require additional high-fidelity validation.
paper_title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework
